html:
SMTO-EXE-0090 — SMTO's screen tools aren't working on that computer

GUID: 360ec12b-6904-5521-9286-61e2b65c164b
Slug: screen-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use its screen tools on the computer the Gateway runs on. That computer may be missing a part SMTO needs, or use a system SMTO doesn't support for screenshots. Nothing was captured.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the system on the Gateway's computer: a Mac needs macOS 14 or later, and Linux needs an X11 (Xorg) desktop session. Screenshots only work on these systems, and reinstalling can't add support to an older one.
  2. When no task is using that Gateway, run the Gateway installer again on that computer. Don't delete the Gateway, its pairing or its settings first. Repairing in place restores missing screen parts while keeping the Gateway's link to SMTO.
  3. After the installer finishes without errors, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a New chat. Existing chats keep the Gateway's old list of abilities; a new chat uses the refreshed one.

What success looks like

  • In a new chat, SMTO takes a screenshot on that computer instead of showing this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who installed the Gateway. Turning on the Screen skill doesn't install anything missing, and don't delete the Gateway's settings or browser profiles to start fresh.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's native screen backend is unavailable: no supported capture backend, pixel format, DPI context or allocation, or a native worker or service exception prevented observation (not necessarily an installation defect).

What this means

  • Native capture/display setup lacks a supported backend, pixel format, DPI context or allocation, or a native worker/service exception prevented observation. This category does not prove an installation defect. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Native capture/display setup lacks a supported backend, pixel format, DPI context or allocation, or a native worker/service exception prevented observation. This category does not prove an installation defect.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect screen_runtime and the failed native/worker phase; distinguish unsupported OS/session, missing dependency and runtime capture failure.

How to fix it

  • Inspect screen_runtime and readiness (backend, unavailable_reason) on the selected Gateway. If a platform backend is missing (Linux needs an X11 session with a 24/32-bit TrueColor visual; macOS still capture needs macOS 14 or later; Windows needs per-monitor DPI and GDI), rerun the Gateway's supported installer in place, restart the Gateway once active work has settled and refresh its capabilities. Existing tasks keep their old capability snapshot, so start a new one.
  • Inspect screen_runtime on the selected Gateway. If a supported platform backend is missing, reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. macOS still capture requires macOS 14 or later; Linux capture requires a supported X11 session. Reinstallation does not change OS support or grant screen permissions.
  • If installation repair is indicated: From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended supported session reports ready and completes the explicit observation.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
